Folks, what we are witnessing right now is a shameful collapse of basic order and civic responsibility. On Thursday, we saw workers in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth actually stage a protest outside the Presidential Palace and announce a 24-hour strike. 

Let's call this what it is: these agitators are demanding legally binding job security guarantees, completely turning their backs on personal responsibility and ignoring the fact that the government has already delivered on the most significant demands. Instead of respecting authority and maintaining stability, these groups are choosing to disrupt the system and undermine the foundational duties of our public institutions. 

When people abandon their duty and demand unconditional guarantees instead of earning their place through honest work, it strikes right at the heart of our traditional values and the fabric of our society. This is a total collapse of respect for governance and the rule of law, and we must stand firm against it.

We are watching a complete breakdown of civic duty and respect for authority right before our eyes. On Thursday, workers in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth decided to stage a protest outside the Presidential Palace and announce a 24-hour strike. 

Let's call these agitators what they are. Instead of showing personal responsibility and respecting the government—which has already delivered on the most significant demands—these people are demanding legally binding job security guarantees. They are choosing to disrupt the system and undermine the foundational duties of our public institutions.

This kind of behavior strikes right at the heart of our traditional values and the fabric of our society. When individuals abandon their duty and demand unconditional guarantees instead of earning their place through honest work, it shows a total collapse of respect for governance and the rule of law. We must stand firm against this kind of chaos.

Folks, what we are witnessing right now is a shameful collapse of basic order and civic responsibility. On Thursday, we saw workers in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth actually stage a protest outside the Presidential Palace and announce a 24-hour strike. 

Let's call this what it is: these agitators are demanding legally binding job security guarantees, completely turning their backs on personal responsibility and ignoring the fact that the government has already delivered on the most significant demands. Instead of respecting authority and maintaining stability, these groups are choosing to disrupt the system and undermine the foundational duties of our public institutions. 

When people abandon their duty and demand unconditional guarantees instead of earning their place through honest work, it strikes right at the heart of our traditional values and the fabric of our society. This is a total collapse of respect for governance and the rule of law, and we must stand firm against it.

source_text:
Let’s look at what is really happening here, because the establishment narrative wants you to blame the workers, but this is a classic case of vulnerable laborers being forced to stand up for their dignity against institutional neglect. On Thursday, workers in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth courageously took to the streets to protest outside the Presidential Palace and announced a 24-hour strike. 

What the elites call "agitation" is actually an essential fight for labor rights and basic survival. These workers are simply demanding legally binding job security guarantees in a system that precarious employment has left unprotected and marginalized. The government claims it has delivered on demands, but systemic inequality and historical job insecurity cannot be wiped away by empty promises from those in power. 

Instead of respecting authority that protects corporate and bureaucratic interests at the expense of working people, these groups are right to disrupt a failing system and demand accountability from public institutions. When workers have to strike just to secure their livelihoods, it exposes the deep structural exploitation at the heart of our society. This isn't a collapse of civic responsibility—it is a long-overdue demand for justice, and we must stand firm in solidarity with them.
